title: Does an epipolar gate help bundle adjustment under the mismatch mix a real SIFT matcher produces?
lede: feeding sensing-matchreal's measured SIFT mismatch mixes into the sensing-epigate trial, gate plus Cauchy beats a RANSAC start at ratio tests of 0.7 and 0.6 (24-seed medians 0.0036 against 0.0052 object radii at 0.7), is ahead but not established at 0.8 and ties at 0.9; synthetic geometry, 24 seeds
summary: sensing-epigate found a fundamental-matrix gate no better than a RANSAC start against invented mismatches; sensing-matchreal then measured real SIFT mismatches on a Middlebury stereo pair. This project runs the epigate trial with each measured mix (rate and along/near/far shares at ratio tests none, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6). Over 24 seeds, gate plus Cauchy adjustment has median error 0.0036 and 0.0029 object radii at ratio 0.7 and 0.6, against 0.0052 and 0.0040 for a RANSAC start (the gate wins 20 and 19 of 24 seeds). At 0.8 it is ahead but not established (0.0084 against 0.0106, 17 of 24, intervals overlap); at 0.9 the two tie (0.057 against 0.071, 11 of 24) and with no ratio test nothing works. An all-uniform control at the same rates gives the same ordering, so the gain is not specific to the measured mix. Limits: one scene and detector for the mix, synthetic orbit geometry, along-epipolar errors measured on a stereo pair but applied across a 12-view orbit, independent draws, untuned gate.
